## `.claude/skills/typesafe-ai/SKILL.md`
````md
---
name: typesafe-ai
license: MIT
description: >
  TypeSafe integration craft for System One models (sometimes called Decision Models) such as Jev,
  which answer typed questions about text, images, and application state with calibrated
  probabilities. Use when building, reviewing, or debugging code that calls TypeSafe; when writing
  its questions or state; when replacing an LLM prompt-and-parse step, keyword matching, or a
  brittle heuristic with a typed question; or when brainstorming where programmable common sense
  fits in an app.
---

# Build with TypeSafe

TypeSafe's **Jev**, the first public **System One model**, answers typed questions about state your
application supplies. State is the text, images, and application data your code sends with a
request. Jev can answer a Choice among options, a Noul (the probability that a statement is true), a
Score on levels you describe, or a Box that locates something in an image. Each answer comes back as
typed data with calibrated probabilities, for your code to use.

The rest of this skill is guidance: patterns that tend to produce reliable integrations. None of it
is absolute. Models change, applications differ, and edge cases exist. When a situation calls for
something else, test the alternative and use your judgment.

## Judgments from Jev, decisions in code

Integrations tend to work best when Jev makes the judgments and code decides what to do with
them. Think of each decision as a **truth table**. Jev supplies the inputs, such as "Does the
customer sound frustrated?" or "Which product is the message about?". Code holds the logic that
maps those inputs to an action.

A question that asks Jev to make the decision, such as "Should this ticket be escalated?" or "What
should the agent do next?", usually means the question is at the wrong layer. Instead, break the
decision into the judgments it depends on, and write the decision itself in code, where it's
visible and testable. Writing out the table often shows gaps in the business logic too. A
combination of judgments with no defined outcome is a design question about the system, and it is
best settled in code.

## Live docs

The live docs are the source of truth for request syntax, SDKs, question types, limits, and current
model behavior. Read the relevant pages as part of the task.

- Start at the [documentation index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt). Append `.md` to a page
  path to get the page as Markdown, and resolve relative links against `https://docs.typesafe.ai`.
- Exact request and response schemas: the [OpenAPI spec](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) and
  the [HTTP API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/api.md) page. For an SDK, see the
  [Python](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/python-sdk.md) or
  [JavaScript](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/js-sdk.md) page and the types in the installed package.
- Question types: [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/primitives.md) and each type's own page,
  [structured instructions and criteria](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/advanced.md), and
  [images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/images.md).
- Models, context limits, and rate limits: [models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/models.md). Known
  model weak spots and their workarounds are on the
  [jaggedness page](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/jaggedness.md).
- Architecture: [how to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/how-to-build.md),
  [patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/patterns.md), and
  [cookbooks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/cookbooks.md). The cookbook closest to your use case is a
  good starting point for a new workflow.

If you can't reach the live docs, use the installed SDK's types or local docs, and tell the user
you did. Leave out details that depend on the version rather than guessing them.

## Workflow

1. **Start from the decision logic.** Begin with what the application will show, select, change,
   or hand off. Sketch the truth table or rules that decide it, and list the inputs they need.
   Inputs that need an understanding of language or images make good questions. Arithmetic, dates,
   exact lookups, and policy usually belong in code. Aim for every question to feed the table, and
   give every combination of answers an outcome, including the case where a Noul lands between your
   thresholds. If code alone can already make the decision reliably, tell the user.
2. **Keep all question wording in one place.** Questions, options, criteria, and thresholds are the
   parts of an integration people audit and edit most. Keeping them together in one module makes
   that easier. [Design the state](#design-the-state) and
   [Write the questions](#write-the-questions) describe what tends to work.
3. **Probe the live API**: send test requests as described in
   [Test with the live API](#test-with-the-live-api). Use representative cases, hard cases, and
   negative cases. Keep going until the application behaves as intended.
4. **Integrate.** A few habits help here. Expose or log the exact request payload. When a call to
   the API fails, surface it as an error, not as an answer; for example, don't treat a failed call
   as a "no". Keep API keys on the server.

If the user's request is open-ended, offer the few directions from [Cookbooks](#cookbooks) that
best serve their goal, and recommend one. If the request is concrete, build it.

## Design the state

A useful check for any question is the **human test**: could a smart person, shown only this state
and this question, answer quickly by intuition? When a question fails the test, the fix is usually
in the state, not in the wording.

- **Give what a person would look at.** That means who sent each message, the full thread rather
  than a truncated last line, names rather than raw IDs or @-mention markup, and the item the
  question is about rather than the whole catalogue. State facts your code already knows, such as
  "all messages in `replies` were sent after the refund was issued", rather than leaving the model
  to work them out again.
- **Supply facts the model may lack**, such as what an internal product name or codename refers
  to.
- **Ensure every field in the state is relevant.** Irrelevant detail clutters the context and
  reduces accuracy. A field added for one question can sway the answer to another, and the model
  can read an empty list as a signal.
- **Be mindful when truncating.** Truncate long strings only when you need to, and check that the
  cut doesn't remove context the questions need.
- **Structure with named fields.** JSON objects with descriptive keys work better than a string of
  serialized JSON. They also let a question refer to each part by its path. Stable names such as
  `candidates.refund_policy` are easier to refer to than array positions.
- **Consider leaving out what no person could judge**, such as an unreadable crop or a distinction
  experts dispute. The model's answer there tends to be noise, and code will treat that noise as
  signal.

## Write the questions

Break complex judgments or decisions into their parts, and combine the answers in code with
weighted sums, boolean logic, thresholds, or other heuristics to reach the final decision. For
example, rather than asking "Is this fraud?" or "Is this spam?", ask the set of atomic questions
about what might make something fraud or spam. Each question tends to work best when it asks for
**one judgment** that a person could make at a glance.

- **Ask the concrete, observable thing.** Aim for something a person could point to: "Is a SQL
  query built by string concatenation here?" rather than "Are there SQL injection risks?".
- **One judgment per question; beware the "or".** Two conditions joined by "or" or "and" usually
  work better as two questions. Likewise, a list of rules usually works better as one question per
  rule.
- **Anchor intent to the goal.** When the judgment is about what someone wants, it helps to name
  their goal: "Which of these files does the user want copied?" rather than "Which of these names
  the main input?".
- **Name the subject directly.** "Where is the coffee mug in `photo`?" reads better than "Where is
  `target` in `photo`?" with the target defined somewhere else. Context that only one question
  needs, including an image, usually fits best in that question's instructions (the question text)
  or its criteria (the descriptions of its options, its levels, or what yes and no mean). Context
  that many questions share can go in the state once, and each question can refer to it by its
  exact path in backticks. When you ask the same question about many items, it usually works better
  to put each item into its own question than to give an ID the model has to look up in a shared
  list.
- **Each question is answered on its own.** Questions in a request can't see each other or each
  other's answers. Any context a question relies on belongs in the state or in that question.
- **Write plainly.** A question isn't an LLM prompt. Preambles, "consider X, Y, and Z" lists, and
  output-format instructions add noise. Descriptions of the options belong in the criteria, not in
  the question. Phrase the question so that a true answer means yes. Watch for double negatives,
  and for presuppositions such as "the next step".
- **Name the case that causes confusion.** If answers keep mixing up two outcomes, say in the
  criteria what separates them, using the specific case. For example, for "Is this a refund
  request?", note that a question about the refund policy is not a request. A vague exclusion such
  as "not other kinds of message" helps less, and can draw attention to the wrong answer.

### Criteria

- **Ask about the null case separately.** A Box always returns a location and a Choice always picks
  an option, even when nothing fits. Pair either one with a Noul in the same request that asks
  whether anything fits ("Is there a coffee mug in `photo`?", "Does `message` name any of our
  products?"), so code can tell when nothing does. As of Jev 1.14, this companion Noul usually works
  better than a "none of the above" option.
- **Option names are sent to the model; question IDs are not.** Names that describe the content
  (`refund_request`, `shipping_delay`) help the model. Positional names (`A`, `left`, `option_1`)
  give it nothing meaningful to go on and can bias the answer.
- **Keep options distinct and concrete.** Wording that options share with each other, or with the
  input, can pull probability toward those options. An option that covers several meanings is
  often worth splitting, because its probability can't tell code which meaning applied. Direction
  and magnitude usually work better as separate questions, so that the answer to one doesn't get
  mixed into the other.
- **Describe each Score level as a situation.** Each level should make sense when read on its own:
  "The customer mentions a minor inconvenience" rather than "More upset than the previous level".
- **Describe a Noul's `false` criterion as a concrete situation**, such as "the package arrived on
  time", rather than as "not late".
- **Use a Noul per statement when more than one can be true.** A Choice picks one option, so a
  message that is both a refund request and a complaint forces it to split probability between the
  two. Separate Nouls let each one be true on its own.

## Compose requests

**Bundle questions that share state.** A handy heuristic: if two calls would send the same state
with different questions, they can likely be one call. Questions are cheap and run in parallel, and
the state is read and paid for once. See
[parallel questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md).

**Ask speculatively**, meaning ask a question before you know whether you'll need its answer. A
question that only matters in some cases can go in the same request as the question that
identifies the case. Ask "Is `order` a return request?" and "Which item in `order.items` is being
returned?" together, and have code read the second answer only when the first is yes. The second
question doesn't need an "if" clause, because code handles the condition. See
[speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md).

A second request is usually worth it when:

- code needs an answer to build the next state, fetch evidence, or choose the next options;
- a state field needed for one question measurably misleads another;
- different sets of questions need to be cached or versioned separately.

## Read the answers

### Confidence is rarely the gate

Naive implementations often use an answer's `confidence` as the check that decides whether code
acts. Confidence measures how concentrated an answer's probability distribution is, which is not
the same as how likely the answer is to be correct. Think about what the probabilities should look
like in your use case; another calculation over them may suit it better.

### Probabilities and thresholds

- **A probability is the likelihood that an answer is correct.** Jev isn't a calculator for
  probability problems. Ask it for judgments, and do any math on odds or probabilities in code. A
  Noul near 0.5 usually means the state doesn't settle the question.
- **The top answer is a good default**: the Choice's top option, or the Score's position.
- **0.7 and 0.3 make good starting thresholds for a Noul**: above 0.7 reads as yes, below 0.3 as no,
  and the band between means the question isn't settled, which can get its own row in the truth
  table. Adjust them when the application calls for it, and be wary of over-fitting them to a
  handful of test cases.
- **Look at Score distributions.** The Score's position can get pulled toward the middle and hide
  two-peaked answers, so look at the level probabilities before deciding which value your code
  reads.

## Test with the live API

Sending test requests to the live API is a great way to test questions against your data. Ask the
user for permission first. Get a budget for experimentation (TypeSafe is very inexpensive, so a
little can go a very long way), disclose what data will be sent (point out any personal or private
data), and say that their `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` will be used.

- Start with a few representative cases, plus hard ones and some whose answer is "no" or "nothing
  fits".
- Compare wordings by sending each variant as a separate question in one request, over the same
  state.
- Read individual answers, not only aggregates.
- Keep the exact request payload for each case so any result can be rerun.
- Check each change against cases you didn't use while tuning.

Make sure any agent that sends test requests has network access to the API endpoint.

### When an answer looks wrong

Check these, in this order:

1. the payload as actually sent;
2. the state, against the human test;
3. the options and candidates: is the right answer among them?
4. the scope of the questions: can each one be broken down into smaller judgments?
5. the wording.

If a clear question with complete state still gets an answer you're confident is wrong, check the
jaggedness page for the model you're using. It lists known weak spots and how to work around them.
If the behavior isn't listed, the TypeSafe team welcomes examples through the channel linked on
that page. In the meantime, work out an alternative approach with the user that avoids the weak
spot.

### Yellow flags

Typically, a good change is one that makes the definition clearer or improves the state. Check each
change on cases you didn't tune on. Wording written to produce a particular value is **prompt
gymnastics**, and it tends to break on new inputs and on the next model version. Some yellow flags:

- criteria that name specific test items, or that gain a clause for each failing case;
- caveats that explain away a model quirk;
- thresholds fitted to particular cases;
- tests that assert an exact probability;
- code that quietly overrides answers.

The structural fix is usually better state, a separate question, or code.

## Cookbooks

Each of these starting points combines questions to serve one goal. Ideas outside this list are
welcome.

- **Route and fill arguments.** One request identifies what the user is asking for and which
  values go in each argument. Code then calls the handler. See
  [function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md) and
  [intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md).
- **Select instead of generate.** Code finds candidate values or spans of text, the model picks
  the intended one, and code copies or normalizes it. See
  [value extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_cookbook.md),
  [date extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/date_extraction_cookbook.md), and
  [structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md).
- **Find and judge evidence.** Retrieve candidates and ask how relevant each one is. See
  [line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find.md),
  [re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md), and
  [classifying RAG passages](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classifying_rag_passages.md).
- **Turn answers into data.** Score each dimension once, then let code or users change the weights
  and views. If you have labeled outcomes, the answers can become features for a model. See
  [composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and
  [feature discovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md).
- **Verify and escalate.** Check claims or fields against their evidence, and send the cases that
  fail to a person or a reasoning model. See
  [citation checks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md) and
  [extraction cascades](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md).

The TypeSafe team is constantly adding cookbooks of well-tested patterns to the live documentation.
It's a good idea to check the [cookbooks index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/cookbooks.md) for one
that fits the problem you're solving.

````

## `app.py`
````py
"""Bid & Risk Assistant — Streamlit UI. Task 007.

    streamlit run app.py

> It reads a construction tender file, finds the line items that will cost the
> contractor money, and writes the clarification letter he'd otherwise spend
> four hours on.

Lead with that sentence. No vocabulary lesson, no file extensions.

Wired: upload -> parse -> item table -> company sliders -> priced totals ->
the reveal. Still stubbed, and owned by other people:

  * the findings panel lights up when `core/detectors.py` (task 004) lands
  * the export button lights up when `export_rfi.py` (task 006) lands

Both are guarded, so an unfinished module shows a note instead of a traceback.

Fallbacks, in order: live parse -> `data/golden/` fixture -> an honest
"format not supported" with the sample loaded on a button. Degrade visibly
rather than fabricating output.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import html
import os
import re
import tempfile
import traceback
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

from core import (classify, constants, detectors, kalkulation, logic, objects,
                  parser_gaeb90, parser_x83, pricer, stammdaten)
from views import reveal

SAMPLE = constants.REVEAL["blank_boq"]
ANSWER_KEY = constants.REVEAL["answer_key"]
PAGES = ("Tender", "Gruppen & Angebot", "Logic", "Heikle Positionen")

XML_SUFFIXES = (".x83", ".x81", ".x84", ".x86")
GAEB90_SUFFIXES = (".d83", ".d81", ".d84", ".d86")

st.set_page_config(
    page_title="Bid & Risk Assistant",
    layout="wide",
    initial_sidebar_state="expanded",
)


# --- parsing ---------------------------------------------------------------

def parse_path(path: str):
    """Parse by format. Returns (items, remarks). Raises on unknown format."""
    suffix = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if suffix in XML_SUFFIXES:
        return parser_x83.parse(path), parser_x83.parse_remarks(path)
    if suffix in GAEB90_SUFFIXES:
        return parser_gaeb90.parse(path), []
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported format: {suffix or path}")


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def load_from_disk(path: str):
    items, remarks = parse_path(path)
    return [i.as_dict() for i in items], remarks


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def load_from_upload(name: str, payload: bytes):
    """Parse uploaded bytes. Cached on content, so sliders don't re-parse."""
    suffix = os.path.splitext(name)[1] or ".x83"
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=suffix, delete=False) as handle:
        handle.write(payload)
        temp = handle.name
    try:
        items, remarks = parse_path(temp)
        return [i.as_dict() for i in items], remarks
    finally:
        os.unlink(temp)


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def load_reference():
    return pricer.load_reference_prices()


def rehydrate(dicts: list[dict]):
    from core.models import NormalizedItem
    return [NormalizedItem.from_dict(d) for d in dicts]


# --- sections --------------------------------------------------------------

def sidebar_kalkulation() -> stammdaten.Company:
    """The cost base the bottom-up calculation uses.

    These are the parameters the client said a contractor must bring himself:
    *"Maschinenstundensätze hast du aus der Firma gegeben"*. Presets come from
    the bidder profiles in the test database.
    """
    st.sidebar.header("Kalkulationsgrundlage")
    presets = stammdaten.companies()
    names = [c.name for c in presets]
    chosen = presets[names.index(st.sidebar.selectbox("Profil", names))]

    wage = st.sidebar.slider("Mittellohn (€/h)", 35.0, 95.0,
                             float(chosen.mittellohn_eur_h), 0.5)

    # The markup, split into its three parts. Arithmetically a combined number
    # is identical — 15 + 5 is always 20 — but split, the estimator can see
    # which decision costs what: keep the AGK, waive the BGK on a strategic
    # job, set W&G where he wants it.
    st.sidebar.markdown("**Zuschläge**")
    agk = st.sidebar.slider(
        "AGK — Allgemeine Geschäftskosten (%)", 0.0, 30.0,
        float(chosen.agk_pct), 0.5,
        help="Kosten des Unternehmens außerhalb der Baustelle, auf ein "
             "ganzes Jahr gerechnet.")
    bgk = st.sidebar.slider("BGK — Baustellengemeinkosten (%)", 0.0, 20.0,
                            float(chosen.bgk_pct), 0.5)
    wg = st.sidebar.slider("W&G — Wagnis und Gewinn (%)", 0.0, 20.0,
                           float(chosen.wg_pct), 0.5)

    # AGK is an annual figure. A ten-month job carries ten twelfths of it.
    months = st.sidebar.slider(
        "Bauzeit (Monate)", 1.0, 24.0, float(chosen.bauzeit_monate), 1.0,
        help="Nur die AGK werden anteilig umgelegt — BGK und W&G nicht.")

    company = stammdaten.Company(
        chosen.name, wage, chosen.zuschlag_pct, chosen.leistungsfaktor,
        chosen.materialfaktor, chosen.profil,
        agk_pct=agk, bgk_pct=bgk, wg_pct=wg, bauzeit_monate=months,
    )
    st.sidebar.metric("Zuschlag gesamt", f"{company.total_markup_pct:.1f} %")
    if months != 12:
        st.sidebar.caption(
            f"AGK {agk:.1f} % × {months:.0f}/12 = **{company.agk_wirksam_pct:.1f} %** "
            f"— {12 - months:+.0f} Monate gegenüber dem Jahr."
        )

    perf = st.sidebar.slider("Leistungsfaktor", 0.6, 1.6,
                             float(chosen.leistungsfaktor), 0.05,
                             help=">1 = langsamer als die Richtwerte")
    mat = st.sidebar.slider("Materialfaktor", 0.6, 1.6,
                            float(chosen.materialfaktor), 0.05)
    company.leistungsfaktor = perf
    company.materialfaktor = mat
    if chosen.profil:
        st.sidebar.caption(chosen.profil)
    return company


def section_upload(show_controls: bool = True):
    """Upload -> parse. Writes (items, remarks, label) into session state."""
    if show_controls:
        def upload_controls():
            upload = st.file_uploader(
                "Tender-Datei hochladen",
                type=[s.lstrip(".") for s in XML_SUFFIXES + GAEB90_SUFFIXES],
            )
            if st.button("Beispiel-LV laden", type="primary"):
                st.session_state["source"] = ("disk", SAMPLE)
                st.rerun()
            if upload is not None:
                uploaded_source = ("upload", upload.name, upload.getvalue())
                if st.session_state.get("source") != uploaded_source:
                    st.session_state["source"] = uploaded_source
                    st.rerun()

        if st.session_state.get("source"):
            with st.expander("Tender-Datei wechseln"):
                upload_controls()
        else:
            upload_controls()

    source = st.session_state.get("source")
    if not source:
        if show_controls:
            st.info("Lade eine GAEB-Datei hoch oder öffne das Beispiel-LV.")
        else:
            st.info("Wechsle zu „Tender“, um eine GAEB-Datei zu laden.")
        return None

    try:
        if source[0] == "disk":
            raw, remarks = load_from_disk(source[1])
            label = os.path.basename(source[1])
        else:
            raw, remarks = load_from_upload(source[1], source[2])
            label = source[1]
    except ValueError as exc:
        # Known-unknown format. Say so plainly and offer the sample — do not
        # guess at a parse and present fabricated positions as real.
        st.error(f"{exc} — unterstützt werden GAEB X83 und GAEB 90 D83/D84/D86.")
        st.session_state.pop("source", None)
        return None
    except Exception:                                      # noqa: BLE001
        st.error(
            "Die Datei konnte nicht gelesen werden. "
            "Gespeicherte Beispieldaten werden versucht."
        )
        with st.expander("What went wrong"):
            st.code(traceback.format_exc())
        try:
            from scripts.dump_golden import load as load_golden
            items, remarks = load_golden(source[1])
            st.success(f"{len(items)} Positionen aus data/golden/ geladen.")
            return items, remarks, os.path.basename(source[1]) + " (fixture)"
        except Exception:                                  # noqa: BLE001
            st.session_state.pop("source", None)
            return None

    items = rehydrate(raw)
    if not items:
        # Spec-normal, not corruption: a .D84 bid submission can carry price
        # records and no quantity records, because it references the .D83/.D86
        # it was bid against. Say that, rather than showing an empty table.
        st.warning(
            f"**{label} enthält Preise, aber keine Mengen.** Das ist bei einem "
            "Angebot normal: Es verweist auf das zugehörige LV. Bitte lade "
            "stattdessen die Leistungsverzeichnis-Datei."
        )
        st.session_state.pop("source", None)
        return None

    priced_in_file = sum(1 for i in items if i.unit_price is not None)
    if show_controls:
        st.caption(
            f"{len(items)} Positionen aus {label}"
            + (f" — {priced_in_file} davon enthalten bereits Preise" if priced_in_file else "")
            + (f", dazu {len(remarks)} Vertragsvorbemerkungen" if remarks else "")
        )
    return items, remarks, label


def section_items(items):
    """The parsed bill of quantities."""
    st.subheader("Ausgelesene Positionen")
    frame = pd.DataFrame([{
        "OZ": i.key(),
        "Position": i.short_text,
        "Menge": i.quantity,
        "Einheit": constants.normalize_unit(i.unit),
        "Pauschal": "ja" if i.is_lump_sum else "",
    } for i in items])
    st.dataframe(frame, width="stretch", hide_index=True, height="stretch")


def source_document(source):
    """Return the original file name and bytes for the active tender."""
    if source[0] == "upload":
        return source[1], source[2]
    with open(source[1], "rb") as handle:
        return os.path.basename(source[1]), handle.read()


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def source_location(filename: str, payload: bytes, source_ref: str) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """Locate a source item without exposing its raw XML or fixed-width record."""
    suffix = os.path.splitext(filename)[1].lower()
    if suffix in XML_SUFFIXES:
        root = ET.fromstring(payload)
        for element in root.iter():
            local_tag = element.tag.rsplit("}", 1)[-1]
            if (
                local_tag == parser_x83.ITEM_TAG
                and element.attrib.get("ID") == source_ref
            ):
                return f"GAEB-XML · Element-ID {source_ref}", True
        return f"Kein XML-Element mit ID {source_ref} gefunden.", False

    match = re.fullmatch(r"type-21 #(\d+)", source_ref)
    if suffix in GAEB90_SUFFIXES and match:
        target = int(match.group(1))
        lines = payload.decode(
            parser_gaeb90.ENCODING,
            errors="replace",
        ).splitlines()
        records = [
            (line_number, line)
            for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1)
            if line.startswith("21")
        ]
        if 1 <= target <= len(records):
            line_number, _ = records[target - 1]
            return f"GAEB 90 · Datensatz 21 · Zeile {line_number}", True
        return f"Datensatz {source_ref} nicht gefunden.", False

    return "Für dieses Dateiformat ist keine Fundstelle verfügbar.", False


def tender_document_html(
    items,
    remarks: list[str],
    selected_key: str,
    filename: str,
) -> str:
    """Render the parsed source tender as a navigable, highlighted document table."""
    rows = []
    if remarks:
        rows.append(
            '<tr class="section"><th colspan="6">'
            "Vertragsvorbemerkungen</th></tr>"
        )
        for index, remark in enumerate(remarks, start=1):
            rows.append(
                '<tr class="remark"><td colspan="6">'
                f'<strong>Vorbemerkung {index}</strong>'
                f'<div class="long-text">{html.escape(remark)}</div></td></tr>'
            )

    current_section = None
    for item in items:
        if item.section_path != current_section:
            current_section = item.section_path
            section = " › ".join(current_section) or "Ohne Abschnitt"
            rows.append(
                '<tr class="section"><th colspan="6">'
                f'{html.escape(section)}</th></tr>'
            )

        short_text = item.short_text or f"Position {item.oz}"
        long_text = item.long_text or short_text
        if long_text.startswith(short_text):
            long_text = long_text[len(short_text):].lstrip(" ,;:-")
        elif long_text.endswith(short_text):
            long_text = long_text[:-len(short_text)].rstrip(" ,;:-")
        description = f"<strong>{html.escape(short_text)}</strong>"
        if long_text:
            description += f'<div class="long-text">{html.escape(long_text)}</div>'
        if item.is_lump_sum:
            description += '<div class="flag">Pauschalposition</div>'

        selected = " selected" if item.key() == selected_key else ""
        row_id = ' id="selected-position"' if selected else ""
        rows.append(
            f'<tr class="position{selected}"{row_id}>'
            f'<td class="oz">{html.escape(item.oz)}</td>'
            f'<td class="description">{description}</td>'
            f'<td class="number">{item.quantity:g}</td>'
            f'<td>{html.escape(item.unit)}</td>'
            f'<td class="number">{_price(item.unit_price)}</td>'
            f'<td class="number">{_price(item.total_price)}</td>'
            "</tr>"
        )

    return f"""<!doctype html>
    <html lang="de">
      <head>
        <meta charset="utf-8">
        <style>
          * {{ box-sizing: border-box; }}
          body {{ margin: 0; color: #172033; background: #fff;
                 font: 14px/1.45 Arial, sans-serif; }}
          .file-name {{ padding: 12px 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid #cbd5e1;
                        font-weight: 700; }}
          table {{ width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; table-layout: fixed; }}
          thead {{ position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 2; }}
          th {{ padding: 9px 10px; text-align: left; background: #e8edf4;
                border-bottom: 1px solid #cbd5e1; }}
          td {{ padding: 9px 10px; vertical-align: top;
                border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }}
          th:nth-child(1) {{ width: 11%; }}
          th:nth-child(2) {{ width: 53%; }}
          th:nth-child(3) {{ width: 9%; }}
          th:nth-child(4) {{ width: 8%; }}
          th:nth-child(5), th:nth-child(6) {{ width: 9.5%; }}
          .section th {{ padding: 11px 10px; color: #334155;
                         background: #f1f5f9; border-top: 1px solid #cbd5e1; }}
          .remark td {{ padding: 12px 14px; background: #fff;
                        border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0; }}
          .position:nth-child(even) {{ background: #fafbfd; }}
          .position.selected td {{ background: #fff3bf; }}
          .position.selected td:first-child {{ border-left: 4px solid #d59b00;
                                                font-weight: 700; }}
          .long-text {{ margin-top: 4px; white-space: pre-wrap; }}
          .number {{ text-align: right; white-space: nowrap; }}
          .flag {{ margin-top: 5px; font-size: 12px; color: #64748b; }}
        </style>
      </head>
      <body>
        <div class="file-name">{html.escape(filename)} · Leistungsverzeichnis</div>
        <table aria-label="Originale GAEB-Positionen">
          <thead><tr>
            <th>OZ</th><th>Leistungstext</th><th>Menge</th>
            <th>Einheit</th><th>EP</th><th>Gesamt</th>
          </tr></thead>
          <tbody>{''.join(rows)}</tbody>
        </table>
        <script>
          document.getElementById("selected-position")?.scrollIntoView(
            {{block: "center"}}
          );
        </script>
      </body>
    </html>
    """


def _price(value: float | None) -> str:
    return f"€{value:,.2f}" if value is not None else "—"


@st.dialog("Originales Leistungsverzeichnis", width="large")
def show_position_details(
    item,
    items,
    remarks: list[str],
    filename: str,
    payload: bytes | None,
    source_error: str | None,
):
    """Show the entire source tender with the matching position highlighted."""
    location = item.source_ref or "Keine Quellreferenz vorhanden."
    if source_error:
        st.warning(f"Quelldokument konnte nicht geöffnet werden: {source_error}")
    elif payload is not None and item.source_ref:
        location, found = source_location(filename, payload, item.source_ref)
        if not found:
            st.info("Die Position ist in den geparsten Daten enthalten, "
                    "aber keine genaue Fundstelle wurde gefunden.")
    else:
        st.info("Für diese Position ist keine genaue Fundstelle verfügbar.")
    st.caption(f"{filename} · {len(items)} Positionen · Fundstelle: {location}")
    st.iframe(
        tender_document_html(items, remarks, item.key(), filename),
        height=600,
        alt=f"Leistungsverzeichnis aus {filename}, Position {item.oz} markiert",
    )


def section_groups(items, assignments, data, filename: str, remarks: list[str],
                   calculated=None):
    """List trade groups; opening one shows the positions in that trade."""
    rows = objects.by_trade(items, assignments, data)
    if calculated:
        stats = kalkulation.summarize(calculated)
        a, b, c = st.columns(3)
        a.metric("Angebotssumme", f"€{stats['total_mid']:,.0f}",
                 help="Mittelwert der Spanne")
        b.metric("Spanne", f"€{stats['total_low']:,.0f} – "
                 f"{stats['total_high']:,.0f}")
        c.metric("Kalkuliert", f"{stats['coverage_pct']:.0f}%",
                 help=f"{stats['unpriced']} Positionen ohne zugeordnete Leistung")

    selected_key = st.session_state.get("selected_group_key")
    selected = next((row for row in rows if row.key == selected_key), None)

    if selected is None:
        st.caption(f"{len(rows)} Gruppen · {len(items)} Positionen")
        query = st.text_input("Gruppe suchen", placeholder="Gewerk")
        query = query.casefold().strip()
        visible_rows = [row for row in rows if query in row.obj.casefold()]
        if not visible_rows:
            st.info("Keine passende Gruppe gefunden.")
            return

        with st.container(key="group_list"):
            for index, row in enumerate(visible_rows):
                with st.container(border=True):
                    name, details, action = st.columns(
                        [5, 2.5, 2],
                        vertical_alignment="center",
                    )
                    name.markdown(f"**{row.obj}**")
                    name.caption(f"{len(row.positions)} Positionen")
                    details.caption(f"Einheiten: {row.unit or '—'}")
                    if action.button(
                        "Öffnen →",
                        key=f"open_group_{index}",
                        width="stretch",
                    ):
                        st.session_state["selected_group_key"] = row.key
                        st.session_state.pop("group_positions", None)
                        st.session_state.pop("opened_position_key", None)
                        st.rerun()
        return

    if st.button("← Alle Gruppen"):
        st.session_state.pop("selected_group_key", None)
        st.session_state.pop("group_positions", None)
        st.session_state.pop("opened_position_key", None)
        st.rerun()
    st.subheader(selected.obj)
    st.caption(
        f"{len(selected.positions)} Positionen · "
        f"Einheiten: {selected.unit or '—'}"
    )
    item_by_key = {item.key(): item for item in items}
    group_items = [item_by_key[key] for key in selected.positions if key in item_by_key]
    st.caption("Klicke auf eine Position, um alle Details und ihre Fundstelle zu öffnen.")
    event = st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame([{
        "OZ": item.key(),
        "Position": item.short_text,
        "Menge": item.quantity,
        "Einheit": constants.normalize_unit(item.unit),
        "Pauschal": "ja" if item.is_lump_sum else "",
    } for item in group_items]),
        width="stretch",
        hide_index=True,
        height="stretch",
        column_config={
            "OZ": st.column_config.TextColumn("OZ", width="small"),
            "Position": st.column_config.TextColumn("Position", width="large"),
            "Menge": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Menge", width="small"),
            "Einheit": st.column_config.TextColumn("Einheit", width="small"),
            "Pauschal": st.column_config.TextColumn("Pauschal", width="small"),
        },
        key="group_positions",
        on_select="rerun",
        selection_mode="single-row",
    )
    selected_rows = event.selection.rows
    if selected_rows:
        row_index = selected_rows[0]
        if 0 <= row_index < len(group_items):
            item = group_items[row_index]
            if st.session_state.get("opened_position_key") != item.key():
                st.session_state["opened_position_key"] = item.key()
                source = st.session_state.get("source")
                payload = None
                source_error = None
                if source:
                    try:
                        filename, payload = source_document(source)
                    except OSError as exc:
                        filename = item.source_file or "Quelldokument"
                        source_error = str(exc)
                else:
                    filename = item.source_file or "Quelldokument"
                    source_error = "Keine Quelldatei im aktuellen Sitzungskontext."
                show_position_details(
                    item,
                    items,
                    remarks,
                    filename,
                    payload,
                    source_error,
                )
    else:
        st.session_state.pop("opened_position_key", None)


def section_kalkulation(calculated, cov, data):
    """Bottom-up Aufschlagskalkulation — the bid. Returns calculated items."""
    stats = kalkulation.summarize(calculated)

    a, b, c, d = st.columns(4)
    a.metric("Angebotssumme", f"€{stats['total_mid']:,.0f}",
             help="Mittelwert der Spanne")
    b.metric("Spanne", f"€{stats['total_low']:,.0f} – {stats['total_high']:,.0f}")
    c.metric("Kalkuliert", f"{stats['coverage_pct']:.0f}%",
             help=f"{stats['unpriced']} Positionen ohne zugeordnete Leistung")
    d.metric("davon Lohn", f"€{stats['labour_eur']:,.0f}")

    if cov["pct"] < 50:
        st.error(
            f"**Nur {cov['pct']}% der Positionen konnten einer Leistung "
            f"zugeordnet werden.** Der Katalog hat "
            f"{len(data.leistungen)} Einträge; dieses LV beschreibt Arbeiten, "
            "die darin nicht vorkommen. Die Summe oben deckt deshalb nur einen "
            "Teil des Leistungsverzeichnisses ab — sie ist kein vollständiges "
            "Angebot. Ein größerer Katalog oder ein semantischer Klassifikator "
            "behebt das; Stichwortabgleich reicht hier nicht."
        )
    if data.is_synthetic:
        st.caption(
            "⚠️ Die Stammdaten sind **synthetisch** (eigene Schätzungen in "
            "ARH-Größenordnung, keine Marktabfrage). Das Verfahren ist echt, "
            "die Zahlen sind Platzhalter, bis echte Firmenwerte hinterlegt sind."
        )

    st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame([{
        "OZ": c.item.key(),
        "Position": c.item.short_text[:52],
        "Menge": c.item.quantity,
        "Einheit": constants.normalize_unit(c.item.unit),
        "Leistung": c.leistung.code if c.leistung else "—",
        "EP min": c.ep_low, "EP mittel": c.ep_mid, "EP max": c.ep_high,
        "GP": c.total,
        "Grundlage": c.note[:60],
    } for c in calculated]), width="stretch", hide_index=True, height="stretch")
    return calculated


def section_tricky(calculated):
    """Show unpriced positions and material pricing risks."""
    st.caption(
        "Gezeigt werden nicht kalkulierbare Positionen, große Kostenspannen "
        "und Pauschalpositionen. Bezifferbare Risiken stehen nach €-Spanne "
        "sortiert; bei nicht kalkulierbaren Positionen ist der Betrag unbekannt."
    )
    rows = []
    for c in calculated:
        reasons = []
        if not c.priced:
            reasons.append("nicht kalkulierbar")
        elif c.band_width > 0.35:
            reasons.append(f"Preisspanne ±{100*c.band_width/2:.0f}%")
        if c.item.is_lump_sum:
            reasons.append("Pauschalposition")
        if not reasons:
            continue
        rows.append({
            "OZ": c.item.key(), "Position": c.item.short_text[:58],
            "Menge": c.item.quantity,
            "Einheit": constants.normalize_unit(c.item.unit),
            "€ unsicher": round(c.euro_at_stake, 2) if c.priced else None,
            "Grund": ", ".join(reasons),
            "_unpriced": not c.priced,
            "_band_width": c.band_width,
            "_lump_sum": c.item.is_lump_sum,
        })
    if not rows:
        st.success("Keine auffällig unsicheren Positionen.")
        return
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values(
        ["_unpriced", "€ unsicher", "_band_width", "_lump_sum"],
        ascending=[True, False, False, False],
    ).head(25)
    frame.insert(0, "Rang", range(1, len(frame) + 1))
    st.markdown(f"**Top {len(frame)} nach Risiko**")
    st.dataframe(
        frame.drop(columns=["_unpriced", "_band_width", "_lump_sum"]),
        width="stretch",
        hide_index=True,
        height="stretch",
    )


def section_pricing(items, company, reference):
    """Comparable-price cross-check. Secondary to the calculation above."""
    st.subheader("7 · Quercheck gegen echte Angebotspreise")
    st.caption(
        "A second, independent estimate from 720 unit prices in three real "
        "submitted bids. Where the two engines agree, confidence is higher; "
        "where they diverge, look. Measured on its own (answer key held out) "
        "this engine is −50% on the total, so it is a cross-check, not a bid."
    )
    priced = pricer.price_boq(items, reference, company)
    stats = pricer.summarize(priced)

    a, b, c, d = st.columns(4)
    a.metric("Estimated total", f"€{stats['total']:,.0f}")
    b.metric("Priced from real bids", f"{stats['benchmark_share_pct']:.0f}%")
    c.metric("No comparable", stats["no_comparable"],
             help="Positions we refuse to price rather than invent a number for.")
    d.metric("On fallback rates", f"€{stats['fallback_value']:,.0f}",
             help="Value resting on hand-authored rates, not observed prices.")

    frame = pd.DataFrame([{
        "OZ": p.item.key(),
        "Position": p.item.short_text[:60],
        "Menge": p.item.quantity,
        "Einheit": constants.normalize_unit(p.item.unit),
        "EP €": p.unit_price if p.unit_price is not None else None,
        "GP €": p.total if p.total is not None else None,
        "Quelle": {
            "benchmark_match": "matched comparable",
            "benchmark": "bucket median",
            "benchmark_unit": "unit median",
            "fallback_rate": "fallback rate",
            "none": constants.NO_COMPARABLE_LABEL,
        }[p.source],
        "Basis": p.note[:70],
    } for p in priced])
    st.dataframe(frame, width="stretch", hide_index=True, height=320)

    if stats["no_comparable"]:
        st.caption(
            f"{stats['no_comparable']} positions print "
            f"“{constants.NO_COMPARABLE_LABEL}”. These are mostly rental and "
            "time-on-site units with nothing comparable in the benchmark. "
            "An honest blank beats an invented euro."
        )
    return priced, stats


def section_findings(priced, remarks):
    """Top findings by € leverage. Lights up when task 004 lands."""
    st.subheader(f"8 · Top {constants.TOP_N_FINDINGS} positions worth arguing about")
    st.caption(
        "Ranked by € leverage (quantity × price exposure). Where no comparable "
        f"exists we print “{constants.NO_COMPARABLE_LABEL}” rather than invent a number."
    )
    try:
        findings = detectors.run_all(priced, remarks, top_n=constants.TOP_N_FINDINGS)
    except NotImplementedError:
        st.info(
            "Detectors are task 004 — not built yet. The pricing above is live; "
            "this panel fills in once `core/detectors.py` is implemented."
        )
        return []

    if not findings:
        st.success("No findings above the detection thresholds.")
        return []

    st.dataframe(pd.DataFrame([{
        "OZ": f.item.key(),
        "Position": f.item.short_text[:60],
        "Detector": f.detector,
        "Severity": f.severity,
        "€ leverage": round(f.euro_leverage, 2),
        "Why": f.rationale,
    } for f in findings]), width="stretch", hide_index=True)
    return findings


def section_reveal(priced, answer, source_label):
    """The reveal. PLAN.md step 4 — this is the whole pitch."""
    st.subheader("9 · How wrong are we?")

    if answer is None:
        st.caption(
            "This tender has no submitted bid to check against. Load the sample "
            "tender to see the comparison that does."
        )
        return

    reveal.render(priced, answer, source_label)


def answer_key_for(label: str):
    """Find a real submitted bid to measure this tender against.

    Two cases exist. The demo blank has a known sibling bid for the same BoQ.
    A file the user uploads may itself be priced (.D84/.D86), in which case it
    is its own answer key — and must then be held out of the benchmark, or we
    would be checking our homework against our own source.
    """
    if label.startswith(os.path.basename(SAMPLE)):
        raw, _ = load_from_disk(ANSWER_KEY)
        return rehydrate(raw), os.path.basename(ANSWER_KEY), os.path.basename(ANSWER_KEY)

    for source in constants_sources():
        if label.startswith(os.path.basename(source)):
            raw, _ = load_from_disk(source)
            return rehydrate(raw), os.path.basename(source), os.path.basename(source)
    return None, "", ""


def constants_sources() -> list[str]:
    """The bids the benchmark was built from, per reference_prices.json."""
    return load_reference().get("meta", {}).get("sources", [])


def section_export(findings):
    """Bieterfragen-Katalog download. Lights up when task 006 lands."""
    st.subheader("10 · The letter")
    if not findings:
        st.button("Export clarification letter (.docx)", disabled=True)
        st.caption("No findings are available for export.")
        return

    import export_rfi
    project = {"title": "Bieterfragen-Katalog"}
    catalog = export_rfi.build_catalog(findings, project)
    if not catalog:
        st.button("Export clarification letter (.docx)", disabled=True)
        st.caption("No findings are available for export.")
        return

    try:
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".docx", delete=False) as handle:
            out_path = handle.name
        export_rfi.to_docx(catalog, out_path, project)
        with open(out_path, "rb") as handle:
            payload = handle.read()
        os.unlink(out_path)
        st.download_button(
            "Export clarification letter (.docx)",
            data=payload,
            file_name="Bieterfragen-Katalog.docx",
            mime="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document",
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        fallback = export_rfi.to_markdown(catalog, project).encode("utf-8")
        st.warning("DOCX export is unavailable; the Markdown fallback is ready.")
        st.download_button(
            "Export clarification letter (.md)",
            data=fallback,
            file_name="Bieterfragen-Katalog.md",
            mime="text/markdown",
        )
        with st.expander("Export details"):
            st.code(str(exc))
````

## `core/classify.py`
````py
"""Position text -> Leistung code. The one job a model is actually good at.

The pricing engine needs to know *what kind of work* a position describes; the
rate table then supplies the hours and the money. Splitting it this way is
deliberate and it is what makes the system defensible:

    classify (hard, fuzzy, language)   -> a model
    price    (easy, exact, arithmetic) -> a lookup

A model asked "how many hours does this take?" produces a plausible number
nobody can check. A model asked "is this Oberboden abtragen or Rohrgraben
aushaeben?" produces an answer that is right or wrong, measurably, against the
106 labelled positions in `Database/`. And because the price then comes from a
table, the same tender always yields the same bid.

Three backends behind one interface:

    cache    on-disk, keyed by text+unit. Checked first, always.
    jev      TypeSafe's classifier: structured label + confidence, cheap.
    keyword  deterministic token overlap. No network, no key, no cost.

`classify()` walks them in that order, so a cold run with no key still works
and a warm run costs nothing. **Pre-generate the cache and commit it** — a
live API call during a demo is a failure mode with no upside.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Iterable, Optional, Sequence

from core.models import NormalizedItem
from core.stammdaten import Leistung, Stammdaten

CACHE_PATH = os.path.join(
    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
    "data", "classification_cache.json",
)

MIN_KEYWORD_SCORE = 0.12     # below this the keyword match is noise
MIN_JEV_CONFIDENCE = 0.35    # below this we would rather say nothing

_STOP = frozenset("""
und oder mit ohne nach vor bis je der die das den dem des ein eine einer
liefern lieferung einbauen herstellen inkl incl einschl gemaess gemäß
""".split())


@dataclass
class Assignment:
    code: Optional[str]
    confidence: float
    source: str          # "cache" | "jev" | "keyword" | "none"
    alternatives: list = None

    def as_tuple(self) -> tuple[Optional[str], float]:
        return (self.code, self.confidence)


# --- shared helpers --------------------------------------------------------

def tokens(text: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    low = re.sub(r"\[?\b(?:person|firma|ort|projekt|nummer|telefon|per)[_0-9]*\]?",
                 " ", (text or "").lower())
    return frozenset(t for t in re.findall(r"[a-zäöüß]{4,}", low) if t not in _STOP)


def fingerprint(item: NormalizedItem, unit: str) -> str:
    """Cache key: the text and unit decide the class, nothing else does."""
    raw = f"{item.short_text}|{item.long_text[:400]}|{unit}".lower()
    return hashlib.sha1(raw.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def candidates(unit: str, data: Stammdaten) -> list[Leistung]:
    """Work types measured in this unit — everything else is impossible.

    The unit is the single strongest signal in a bill of quantities and it is
    free. Restricting to it before any fuzzy matching removes most of the ways
    a classifier can be confidently wrong.
    """
    shortlist = data.by_unit(unit)
    return shortlist or list(data.leistungen.values())


# --- backend: keyword ------------------------------------------------------

def classify_keyword(item: NormalizedItem, data: Stammdaten, unit: str) -> Assignment:
    """Token overlap against each candidate's Taetigkeit and Bemerkung.

    The deterministic floor. It has no domain knowledge and will never beat a
    real classifier, but it costs nothing, runs offline, and makes the whole
    system work with no API key at all.
    """
    item_tokens = tokens(f"{item.short_text} {item.long_text[:400]}")
    if not item_tokens:
        return Assignment(None, 0.0, "none")

    scored = []
    for leistung in candidates(unit, data):
        ref = tokens(f"{leistung.taetigkeit} {leistung.bemerkung} {leistung.gewerk}")
        if not ref:
            continue
        overlap = len(item_tokens & ref)
        if not overlap:
            continue
        scored.append((overlap / len(item_tokens | ref), leistung.code))

    if not scored:
        return Assignment(None, 0.0, "none")
    scored.sort(reverse=True)
    best_score, best_code = scored[0]
    if best_score < MIN_KEYWORD_SCORE:
        return Assignment(None, round(best_score, 3), "none",
                          [c for _, c in scored[:3]])
    return Assignment(best_code, round(best_score, 3), "keyword",
                      [c for _, c in scored[:3]])


# --- backend: Jev ----------------------------------------------------------

def _load_env_once() -> None:
    """Read `.env` into the environment if the key is not already set.

    Streamlit does not load `.env`, so without this the app silently has no
    API key, falls back to keyword matching and reports ~3% coverage on any
    file that is not already cached. Stdlib only — no python-dotenv.
    """
    if os.getenv("JEV_KEY") or os.getenv("JEV_API_KEY"):
        return
    path = os.path.join(
        os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), ".env")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
                    continue
                name, value = line.split("=", 1)
                os.environ.setdefault(name.strip(), value.strip())
    except OSError:
        pass


def jev_available() -> bool:
    _load_env_once()
    return bool(os.getenv("JEV_KEY") or os.getenv("JEV_API_KEY"))


JEV_URL = os.getenv("JEV_URL", "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone")
JEV_MODEL = os.getenv("JEV_MODEL", "jev-latest")
# The decision rule, measured against representative and negative cases.
# Probed on real positions plus two deliberate negatives ("Teppichboden
# verlegen", "Dachabdichtung aufschweißen" — trades absent from this
# catalogue). Both negatives scored noul<=0.07 AND option probability <=0.35;
# genuine matches scored 0.62-0.99 on the option. So:
#
#     accept if  p >= 0.60                      (the option is clearly right)
#            or  p >= 0.45 and noul >= 0.60     (plausible and the catalogue
#                                                does contain this kind of work)
#
# `confidence` is deliberately unused: it measures how peaked the distribution
# is, not how likely the answer is to be correct.
STRONG_OPTION_PROB = 0.60
WEAK_OPTION_PROB = 0.45
MIN_MATCH_NOUL = 0.60


class JevError(RuntimeError):
    """A failed call is an error, never an answer.

    Treating an outage as "no match" would silently drop positions out of the
    bid and look like a clean result. The caller decides whether to fall back
    to the keyword backend; this layer does not decide for it.
    """


def _slug(text: str) -> str:
    """Descriptive option name. Jev sees these, so they carry meaning.

    Positional names (`option_1`) give the model nothing to reason about, and
    the Leistung codes (`E01`) are equally meaningless to it. The activity
    text is what a person would read.
    """
    base = re.sub(r"[^a-zäöüß0-9]+", "_", (text or "").lower()).strip("_")
    return base[:60] or "unbenannt"


def classify_jev(
    item: NormalizedItem,
    data: Stammdaten,
    unit: str,
    timeout: float = 30.0,
) -> Assignment:
    """Ask Jev which Leistung this position describes.

    Two questions in one request, sharing one state:

      `passt`     a Noul — does the catalogue contain this work at all?
      `leistung`  a Choice — which entry, given that it does

    The Noul is not optional. A Choice *always* returns an option, even when
    nothing fits, so without a companion Noul every unrelated position would
    be confidently assigned a wrong Leistung and silently mis-priced. The
    catalogue has 34 entries and a real tender contains work that is simply
    not in it, so "none of these" is the common case, not the edge case.

    Code, not the model, decides what to do with the two judgments.
    """
    import urllib.request

    key = os.getenv("JEV_KEY") or os.getenv("JEV_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        raise JevError("JEV_KEY is not set")

    # The whole catalogue, not the unit shortlist. Measured: restricting by
    # unit HIDES the right answer — "Sanitärcontainer aufstellen" is billed in
    # St but belongs to Baustelleneinrichtung (psch), so the unit shortlist
    # forced a wrong pick at p=0.71 while the full catalogue found it at 0.99.
    # Worse, a unit with one candidate makes the Choice degenerate: it must
    # return that option at p=1.00 regardless of the text.
    shortlist = list(data.leistungen.values())
    if not shortlist:
        return Assignment(None, 0.0, "none")

    criteria, back = {}, {}
    for leistung in shortlist:
        name = _slug(leistung.taetigkeit)
        while name in back:                       # keep option names unique
            name = f"{name}_{leistung.code.lower()}"
        back[name] = leistung.code
        criteria[name] = (
            f"{leistung.taetigkeit}. Abgerechnet in {leistung.einheit}."
            + (f" {leistung.bemerkung}" if leistung.bemerkung else "")
        )

    payload = {
        "model": JEV_MODEL,
        # The catalogue goes in the state because questions are answered
        # independently: the Noul cannot see the Choice's criteria, so without
        # this it has no idea what "the list" is and returned ~0.78 for
        # everything, including work from entirely different trades.
        "state": {
            "position": {
                "kurztext": item.short_text,
                "langtext": (item.long_text or "")[:1000],
                "einheit": unit,
                "menge": item.quantity,
            },
            "katalog": [f"{l.taetigkeit} [{l.einheit}]" for l in shortlist],
        },
        "questions": {
            "passt": {
                "type": "noul",
                "instructions": (
                    "Lässt sich die Arbeit in `position` mit einer Zeile aus "
                    "`katalog` kalkulieren?"
                ),
                "criteria": {
                    "true": "Eine Katalogzeile beschreibt dieselbe Art von "
                            "Arbeit in derselben Abrechnungseinheit; Material, "
                            "Dimension oder Fabrikat dürfen abweichen.",
                    "false": "Der Katalog enthält keine Zeile für diese Art von "
                             "Arbeit, etwa weil sie zu einem anderen Gewerk "
                             "gehört.",
                },
            },
            "leistung": {
                "type": "choice",
                "instructions": "Welche Leistung beschreibt `position`?",
                "criteria": criteria,
            },
        },
    }

    request = urllib.request.Request(
        JEV_URL,
        data=json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8"),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json",
                 "Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=timeout) as response:
            body = json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except Exception as exc:                                # noqa: BLE001
        raise JevError(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}") from exc

    answers = body.get("answers", {})
    fits = float(answers.get("passt", {}).get("noul", 0.0))
    choice = answers.get("leistung", {}) or {}
    name = choice.get("choice")
    probabilities = choice.get("probabilities", {}) or {}
    probability = float(probabilities.get(name, 0.0))

    # Code holds the logic. The Noul decides whether anything fits at all; the
    # option's own probability decides whether we know which. `confidence` is
    # deliberately unused — it measures how peaked the distribution is, not
    # how likely the answer is to be right.
    if name not in back:
        return Assignment(None, round(probability, 3), "jev_unsure")
    strong = probability >= STRONG_OPTION_PROB
    plausible = probability >= WEAK_OPTION_PROB and fits >= MIN_MATCH_NOUL
    if not (strong or plausible):
        return Assignment(None, round(probability, 3),
                          "jev_nomatch" if fits < MIN_MATCH_NOUL else "jev_unsure")

    alternatives = sorted(probabilities.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:3]
    return Assignment(
        back[name], round(probability, 3), "jev",
        [f"{back.get(n, n)}:{p:.2f}" for n, p in alternatives],
    )


# --- cache -----------------------------------------------------------------

def load_cache() -> dict:
    if not os.path.exists(CACHE_PATH):
        return {}
    try:
        with open(CACHE_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return json.load(fh)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return {}


def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(CACHE_PATH), exist_ok=True)
    with open(CACHE_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(cache, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1, sort_keys=True)


# --- the interface ---------------------------------------------------------

def classify(
    items: Iterable[NormalizedItem],
    data: Stammdaten,
    use_jev: bool | None = None,
    write_cache: bool = True,
    max_workers: int = 8,
) -> dict[str, tuple]:
    """Assign a Leistung code to every position. `{oz_key: (code, confidence)}`.

    `use_jev=None` (the default) means **call Jev for anything not cached, if a
    key is available**. The cache still answers instantly for the demo tender,
    so the prepared path makes no network call — but an arbitrary file a judge
    uploads is not in the cache, and the keyword fallback scores near zero on
    real tender wording. Refusing to call the API there does not make the demo
    safer, it just reports 3% coverage and looks broken.

    Pass `use_jev=False` to force the offline path.
    """
    from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
    from core import constants

    items = list(items)
    cache = load_cache()
    out: dict[str, tuple] = {}
    misses: list[NormalizedItem] = []

    for item in items:
        hit = cache.get(fingerprint(item, constants.normalize_unit(item.unit)))
        if hit:
            out[item.key()] = (hit.get("code"), float(hit.get("confidence", 0.0)))
        else:
            misses.append(item)

    if use_jev is None:
        use_jev = jev_available()

    def resolve(item: NormalizedItem) -> tuple:
        unit = constants.normalize_unit(item.unit)
        if use_jev:
            try:
                assignment = classify_jev(item, data, unit)
            except JevError:
                assignment = classify_keyword(item, data, unit)
            if assignment.code is not None:
                return item, assignment
        return item, classify_keyword(item, data, unit)

    if misses:
        # Parallel because a judge is watching: 248 positions take ~10s at 8
        # workers and over three minutes one at a time.
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as pool:
            resolved = list(pool.map(resolve, misses))
        for item, assignment in resolved:
            out[item.key()] = assignment.as_tuple()
            cache[fingerprint(item, constants.normalize_unit(item.unit))] = {
                "code": assignment.code,
                "confidence": assignment.confidence,
                "source": assignment.source,
                "text": item.short_text[:90],
            }
        if write_cache:
            save_cache(cache)
    return out


def coverage(assignments: dict) -> dict:
    total = len(assignments)
    hit = sum(1 for code, _ in assignments.values() if code)
    return {"positions": total, "classified": hit,
            "unclassified": total - hit,
            "pct": round(100.0 * hit / total, 1) if total else 0.0}

````

## `core/constants.py`
````py
"""Tunables, inline. No JSON, no load path, no KeyError on stage.

PLAN.md is explicit about this: anything the demo depends on lives in Python
here, so a missing file cannot take the app down mid-presentation. The only
file-loaded data is `data/reference_prices.json` (built from real priced files),
and the pricer must degrade to `kein Vergleichswert` if it is absent.

Rates below are **fallback** values, used only where no real comparable exists,
and the UI must label them as such. PLAN.md flags as unverified whether
hand-authored rates are permitted at all — confirm before leaning on them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# --- Company cost base (the Streamlit sliders) -----------------------------

DEFAULT_COMPANY = {
    "mittellohn_eur_h": 52.0,   # loaded average wage
    "overhead_pct": 12.0,       # Baustellengemeinkosten
    "profit_pct": 5.0,          # Wagnis und Gewinn
    "risk_appetite": 0.5,       # 0 = defensive pricing, 1 = aggressive
}

SLIDER_RANGES = {
    "mittellohn_eur_h": (35.0, 80.0, 0.5),
    "overhead_pct": (0.0, 30.0, 0.5),
    "profit_pct": (0.0, 20.0, 0.5),
    "risk_appetite": (0.0, 1.0, 0.05),
}

# --- Pricing fallbacks ------------------------------------------------------
# Keyed by GAEB unit. Rough Tiefbau/Straßenbau order of magnitude. TODO(pricer
# owner): sanity-check these against the medians that come out of
# data/reference_prices.json and delete any that the real data covers.
FALLBACK_RATES_BY_UNIT: dict[str, float] = {
    "m": 45.0,
    "m2": 38.0,
    "m3": 55.0,
    "st": 120.0,
    "stk": 120.0,
    "psch": 1500.0,
    "h": 52.0,
    "t": 90.0,
    "kg": 3.5,
}

UNIT_ALIASES = {
    "m²": "m2", "qm": "m2", "m³": "m3", "cbm": "m3",
    "stck": "st", "stk": "st", "stück": "st",
    "std": "h", "to": "t", "pausch": "psch",
    # Mixed-encoding repair. These files are cp850 (the umlauts decode
    # correctly) but whatever wrote them emitted the superscripts as latin-1:
    # byte 0xB2 is '²' in latin-1 and '▓' in cp850, 0xB3 is '³' vs '│'. So 50
    # of the 720 priced items arrive as "m▓"/"m│" and would otherwise form
    # their own bogus unit buckets, splitting every area/volume benchmark.
    "m▓": "m2", "m│": "m3",
}

# Units that measure *time-on-site* rather than work done (vorhalten / hire).
# Their unit prices are per-week or per-day and are not comparable with the
# same nominal unit used for installation work.
TIME_RENTAL_UNITS = {"wo", "stwo", "mwo", "m2d", "md", "d", "mt", "jahr"}


def normalize_unit(raw: str) -> str:
    """Canonical unit key: trimmed, lowercased, aliases and encoding repaired."""
    unit = (raw or "").strip().lower()
    return UNIT_ALIASES.get(unit, unit)


# --- Keyword buckets ------------------------------------------------------
# The join dimension for benchmarking, alongside unit. Crude and legible on
# purpose — this gets read out loud in the demo. First match wins, so order
# matters: more specific terms before generic ones. Derived from the actual
# vocabulary of the 720 priced items, not invented.
BUCKET_KEYWORDS: tuple[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]], ...] = (
    ("armatur",      ("absperrschieber", "schieber", "kugelhahn", "flansch",
                      "blindflansch", "hydrant", "armatur")),
    ("formteil",     ("bogen", "muffe", "abgang", "reduzierung", "übergang",
                      "formteil", "anschweiss")),
    ("rohr",         ("rohr", "leitung", "ltg", "dn/od", "verlegen")),
    ("schacht",      ("schacht", "sohle", "sohlen", "abdeckung")),
    ("verbau",       ("verbau", "grabenverbau", "spundwand", "aussteifung")),
    ("erdarbeiten",  ("graben", "boden", "aushub", "verfüllen", "verdichten",
                      "erde", "fördern", "lösen", "planum")),
    ("strasse",      ("asphalt", "pflaster", "fahrbahn", "bordstein", "decke",
                      "tragschicht", "strasse", "straße")),
    ("absicherung",  ("bauzaun", "warnleuchte", "schutzwand", "laufsteg",
                      "absperrung", "sichern", "beschilderung", "absicherung")),
    ("baustelle",    ("baustelleneinrichtung", "standplatz", "vorhalten",
                      "umsetzen", "aufbauen", "abbauen", "räumen")),
    ("dokumentation", ("dokumentation", "foto", "bestandsplan", "aufmass",
                       "aufmaß", "nachweis")),
    ("stundenlohn",  ("stundenlohn", "facharbeiter", "helfer", "vorarbeiter")),
)
BUCKET_FALLBACK = "sonstiges"


def bucket_for_text(text: str) -> str:
    """First matching keyword bucket. Order in BUCKET_KEYWORDS decides ties.

    Lives here, not in the builder script, because the benchmark builder and
    the pricer MUST bucket identically — if they drift, every lookup misses and
    the pricer silently falls through to its fallback rates.
    """
    low = (text or "").lower()
    for bucket, keywords in BUCKET_KEYWORDS:
        if any(k in low for k in keywords):
            return bucket
    return BUCKET_FALLBACK


# --- Company -> price model ------------------------------------------------
# How the sliders move an observed market price. A benchmark median already
# embeds *that* contractor's wage, overhead and margin, so the sliders express
# a ratio against DEFAULT_COMPANY, not an absolute build-up. At
# DEFAULT_COMPANY the multiplier is exactly 1.0 — the baseline estimate is the
# raw benchmark, which is what makes the reveal's error number meaningful.
PRICING_MODEL = {
    "labour_share": 0.35,   # share of a typical Tiefbau rate that is wage
    "risk_span": 0.10,      # +/- swing from the pricing-aggression slider
}

# --- Detector 1: unit-price outlier ----------------------------------------
# Two modes, because the input decides what is detectable:
#
#   priced file (a bid)   -> observed EP vs. the market -> speculative pricing
#   blank tender          -> no EP exists to test. Comparing our own estimate
#                            against the distribution it was drawn from is
#                            circular: 228 of the demo file's 248 estimates
#                            ARE their benchmark median. So on a blank tender
#                            the detectable risk is market *dispersion* — the
#                            positions where comparable contractors disagree
#                            wildly, so our single number is least trustworthy.
OUTLIER_HIGH_FACTOR = 1.6   # observed EP above median x this -> flag
OUTLIER_LOW_FACTOR = 0.6
DISPERSION_WARN_RATIO = 1.0   # (p75-p25)/median above this = wide market spread

# Severity bands, in euro at stake. Shared by all three detectors so "high"
# means the same thing everywhere in the UI.
SEVERITY_HIGH_EUR = 10_000.0
SEVERITY_MEDIUM_EUR = 2_000.0
MIN_COMPARABLES = 3         # below this, print kein Vergleichswert instead

# Nearest-comparable matching (pricer tier 1). Jaccard overlap on item-text
# content tokens. Measured against validate.py's leave-one-out error, not
# guessed. Swept 0.20-0.50: median absolute error stays 7-9% and 70-78% of
# positions land within 30% across the whole range, so this is a plateau rather
# than a tuned point. Requiring 2+ matches is much worse (median error 25-38%)
# because it pushes items back onto the coarse keyword buckets.
MIN_TEXT_SIMILARITY = 0.30
MIN_TEXT_MATCHES = 1        # how many similar lines before we trust the match
NO_COMPARABLE_LABEL = "kein Vergleichswert"

# --- Detector 2: vague scope ----------------------------------------------
# Run over <Remark> / Vorbemerkungen text as well as item text — PLAN.md calls
# the 46 Remark blocks the highest-value target for the least work.
VAGUE_SCOPE_TERMS: dict[str, str] = {
    "nach bedarf": "quantity left open to the client",
    "nach wahl des auftraggebers": "client picks the spec after award",
    "erforderlichenfalls": "scope conditional, unpriceable as written",
    "in abstimmung mit": "scope depends on a later agreement",
    "nebenleistung": "pushed into unpaid incidental work",
    "besondere leistung": "may or may not be separately paid",
    "o. ä.": "equivalent product left undefined",
    "oder gleichwertig": "equivalence judged by the client",
    "bauseits": "dependency on the client's own works",
    "evtl": "contingent scope",
    "ggf": "contingent scope",
    "pauschal": "lump sum absorbs quantity risk",
    "stundenlohnarbeiten": "day-work position, quantity unbounded",
}

# --- Detector 3: quantity / unit sanity -----------------------------------
SUSPICIOUS_ROUND_QUANTITIES = (100.0, 500.0, 1000.0, 5000.0, 10000.0)
PROVISIONAL_SHARE_WARN_PCT = 15.0   # Eventualpositionen share of total value
# Only rules the data actually supports. Each was measured against the 720
# real priced items: the share is how often that keyword really is measured in
# that unit. A rule below ~70% fires on correctly-priced work more often than
# on errors, which is worse than having no rule.
#
# Kept (measured):      boden 82% of 17   verfüllen 100% of 3
# Dropped (measured):   rohr      38% of 42    leitung 31% of 26
#                       asphalt   33% of 3     schacht 100% but n=2
#                       pflaster 100% but n=2  aushub  100% but n=1
#
# `rohr -> m` is the instructive one. It looks obvious and it is wrong: in
# "Kies-Sand-Gemisch Einbettung Rohr DN300-400 verdichten" the pipe is what the
# gravel surrounds, and m3 is the correct basis. The keyword names the subject
# of the position, not how it is measured — only the verb would tell you that.
UNIT_EXPECTED_BY_KEYWORD = {
    "boden": "m3",
    "verfüllen": "m3",
}
UNIT_RULE_MIN_SUPPORT = 0.70   # the bar a rule must clear to be worth keeping

# --- Ranking / display ----------------------------------------------------
TOP_N_FINDINGS = 20         # PLAN.md: top 15-25 by euro leverage
SEVERITY_ORDER = ("high", "medium", "low")

# --- The reveal (PLAN.md step 4, the whole pitch) -------------------------
REVEAL = {
    "blank_boq": "Dataset/[NUMMER_001]_leer.X83",
    "answer_key": "Dataset/StBALV23040.D86",
    "actual_bid_total_eur": 897_305.45,
    "disagreement_threshold_pct": 30.0,
}

GOLDEN_DIR = "data/golden"
REFERENCE_PRICES = "data/reference_prices.json"

````

## `core/detectors.py`
````py
"""Three detectors. Not five.

Each detector is a pure function `(priced_items, context) -> list[Finding]`.
No I/O, no Streamlit, no printing. Findings are ranked by euro leverage
(quantity x price exposure) and the top ~20 are shown.

**What "outlier" means depends on the input, and this is the one thing to
understand before changing detector 1.** A priced file (a submitted bid) has
observed unit prices, so a rate far from the market is a real finding — the
classic speculative-price check. A *blank tender* has no prices at all: the
only number available is our own estimate, and that estimate was drawn from
the benchmark distribution, so testing it against that distribution is
circular. On the demo file 228 of 248 estimates are exactly their benchmark
median; a naive implementation returns zero findings and looks like it works.

So on a blank tender detector 1 reports **dispersion**: the positions where
real contractors disagree most about the rate. Those are where a single number
is least trustworthy and where the money moves.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Optional, Sequence

from core import constants
from core.models import Finding, NormalizedItem
from core.pricer import PricedItem

# A contract clause has no attributable euro value but can outweigh every line
# item in the tender, so remark findings cannot compete on leverage and would
# otherwise never surface. They get reserved slots instead.
REMARK_SLOTS = 3


def severity_for(euro: float) -> str:
    if euro >= constants.SEVERITY_HIGH_EUR:
        return "high"
    if euro >= constants.SEVERITY_MEDIUM_EUR:
        return "medium"
    return "low"


def euro_leverage(item: NormalizedItem, unit_price: Optional[float]) -> float:
    """Quantity x price exposure. The single ranking number."""
    if unit_price is None:
        return 0.0
    return abs(item.quantity * unit_price)


def _synthetic_item(oz: str, text: str) -> NormalizedItem:
    """A stand-in position for findings that belong to no single line.

    Contract preamble and whole-BoQ observations still have to render in a
    table keyed on positions, so they get a labelled pseudo-position rather
    than a `None` the UI would have to special-case.
    """
    return NormalizedItem(oz=oz, quantity=0.0, unit="", short_text=text)


# --- Detector 1 -------------------------------------------------------------

def unit_price_outlier(priced: Sequence[PricedItem]) -> list[Finding]:
    """Speculative prices where prices exist; market dispersion where they don't."""
    findings: list[Finding] = []

    for p in priced:
        dist = p.distribution
        if not dist or dist.get("n", 0) < constants.MIN_COMPARABLES:
            continue
        median = dist.get("median") or 0.0
        if median <= 0:
            continue

        observed = p.item.unit_price

        if observed is not None:
            # The file carries a real submitted rate: test it against the market.
            #
            # Tested against the *quartiles*, not a ratio to the median. Some
            # comparable groups are enormously wide — the catch-all "St" group
            # spans 0.50 to 39,186 EUR — and against a median alone a perfectly
            # ordinary rate in a wide group reads as "0.1x the market". Using
            # the band the comparables actually occupy makes the test as strict
            # as the evidence allows and no stricter.
            low = dist.get("p25", median) * constants.OUTLIER_LOW_FACTOR
            high = dist.get("p75", median) * constants.OUTLIER_HIGH_FACTOR
            if low <= observed <= high:
                continue
````
